New paleomagnetic results from the ca. 1.0 Ga Jiayuan Formation of the
Huaibei Group in the North China craton, and their
paleogeographic implications
Hanqing Zhaoa,b, Shihong Zhanga,b,*, Wangqi Rena, Jikai Dinga, Kunkun Yanga, Haiyan Lia,
Tianshui Yanga, Huaichun Wua, Jianping Chenb
aState Key Laboratory of Biogeology and Environmental Geology, China University of Geosciences, Beijing 100083, China
bSchool of Earth Sciences and Resources, China University of Geosciences, Beijing 100083, China
A R T I C L E I N F O A B S T R A C T
Keywords: The Rodinia supercontinent formed in the transition between Mesoproterozoic and Neoproterozoic. The high-
North China craton quality paleomagnetic poles around 1000 Ma, however, are rather scarce in the global paleomagnetic data-
Jiayuan Formation base, hindering a well-calibrated paleogeographic reconstruction for when and how Rodinia assembled. The late
Transition between Mesoproterozoic and Mesoproterozoic to early Neoproterozoic Huaibei Group strata (ca. 1120–890 Ma) exposed at the southeastern
Neoproterozoic
margin of the North China craton (NCC) provide great promise for paleomagnetism. In this study, we mainly

report a new paleopole (54.2 ◦S, 111.4 ◦E, A95 =5.1◦) obtained from the upper Jiayuan Formation in the middle
Rodinia assembly Huaibei Group by incorporating our new data with the previously published virtual geomagnetic poles. That
average pole passed a positive fold test and a positive reversal test, along with the pole’s distinctiveness from
younger poles of the NCC, support the interpretation that the remanence is primary. New detrital zircon U–Pb
age analyses of a sandstone sample of the Jiayuan Formation and the mafic sills intruding the overlying strata
dated previously together constrain the depositional age of the Jiayuan Formation to be between ca. 1089 and ca.
945 Ma. Our new data, incorporated with other poles previously reported from the Huaibei Group and the mafic
sills intruding the strata, reveal that the NCC underwent large-scale paleolatitudinal shifts from the polar region
to low latitudes across the transition between Mesoproterozoic and Neoproterozoic. Matching the apparent polar
wander paths of the NCC and Laurentia suggests that they together drifted from the polar region in the northern
hemisphere at ca. 1110 Ma to moderate latitudes in the southern hemisphere around 1000 Ma during the as-
sembly of Rodinia.
1. Introduction stage of Rodinia assembly (Swanson-Hysell, 2021; Evans, 2021).

Fig. 3. Detrital zircon geochronologic results. Detrital zircon U–Pb analysis for the quartz sandstone of the Jiayuan Fm shown in (A) Wetherill concordia diagrams
and (B) kernel density estimate (KDE) plots. The grey analyses are outside our concordance limits and are omitted from the KDE plots. See Table S1 for detrital zircon
U–Pb analysis data. The zoomed in figure in A shows the concordia plot focusing on the youngest statistical population. The weighted mean age of four youngest
grains is 1089 ±37 Ma (2σ, MSWD =3.8). The youngest grain is dated at 1063 ±12 Ma (1σ), also providing an estimate of the maximum depositional age. (C)
Representative zircon CL-images and individual analysis results. (For interpretation of the references to colour in this figure legend, the reader is referred to the web
version of this article.)

acquisition curves of the silty limestone from the Jiayuan Formation (Fm). (C) and (D) Magnetic susceptibility (κ/T) curves of the silty limestone from the Jiayuan Fm
and the diabase from the sill #21SZ01, respectively. (For interpretation of the references to colour in this figure legend, the reader is referred to the web version of

rock magnetic results that demonstrate the main magnetic carriers in the
samples are magnetite grains. The ChRM directs southwest with steep
positive inclinations in geographic coordinates (Fig. 5D and 6C) and
directs southwest with moderate negative inclinations after till correc-
tion according to the bedding of the overturned host strata (Fig. 6C;
Table 1). The sample-mean direction of the sill is D =303.9 ◦, I =70.9◦,
k = 87.7, α 95 = 5.5◦ in geographic coordinates and D = 318.0◦, I =
-39.2◦, k = 87.7, α 95 = 5.5◦ in stratigraphic coordinates (Fig. 6C;
Table 1), corresponding to a VGP located at 21.3 ◦N, 339.3 ◦E (dp/dm =
3.9◦/6.6◦). It is shown that the VGP is consistent with those of the ca.
945–920 Ma group mafic sills (Fu et al., 2015; Zhao et al., 2020; Fig. 7;
Table S2), but different from the VGPs of the ca. 890 Ma sills (Fu et al.,
2015; Fig. 7; Table 2). We thus infer that the sill #21SZ01 intruding the
Zhangqu Fm should belong to the older group mafic sills, which con-
strains the Jiudingshan and Zhangqu formations to be older than ca.
945 Ma. We calculated a new pole for the ca. 945–920 Ma sills by
averaging the VGPs obtained from the sill #21SZ01 and six sills in the
Xuzhou and Dalian regions reported previously (Fu et al., 2015; Zhao
et al., 2020). The updated ca. 945–920 Ma pole for the NCC (pole
NC930-2) is located at 27.4 ◦S, 144.5 ◦E (A95 =9.8◦) (Fig. 7), which is
indistinguishable from the previous one (pole NC930 in Table 2; Zhao
et al., 2020) with a small angular separation of 2.4◦ ±9.8◦ (2σ). Our
new NC930-2 pole should supersede the NC930 pole. This pole passed a
bootstrap reversal test at 95% confidence level (Tauxe, 2010; Fig. 7).
